text:
ana: Heads-up — canary evals started failing after the quant bring-up. Not huge, but consistent across runs.

ana: Observed on q8/k on the new kernel build (kernel v3.4.1). Accuracy delta on eval-suite-A: -3.1% vs baseline, threshold is -1.0%.

ana: Quick log snippet from the harness:```\n2026-02-24T14:12:03Z runner INFO evaluating model: open-llama-70b-q8k\n2026-02-24T14:12:04Z evaluator ERROR metric: accuracy_delta = -0.0312 (expected > -0.01)\n2026-02-24T14:12:05Z runner WARN sample variance high: seed=42\n```\n\nci-bot: Canary pipeline reported: https://ci.internal/redwood/canary/1764201123/artifacts (contains raw outputs + token-level diffs).

mike: @ana which commit moved the RNG seeding change? I remember a tiny refactor in sampling for deterministic caching.

ana: I think it was in sampling-service commit 9f3b2a4, merged yesterday by @jules. It changed default deterministic_seed from None -> 0 when caching enabled.

jules: That was intentional to make cache lookups stable, but hmm — didn't test across quantized kernels. I'll run local reproducer now.

jules: Local quick-run:```\n# run minimal harness\npython -m eval_harness.runner --model open-llama-70b-q8k --suite eval-suite-A --seed 0 --num-examples 200\n```\n\njules: Repro: accuracy_delta = -3.0% with seed 0, but with seed randomized (None) we get -0.4%. So seeding seems to shift scores.

mike: Ok that narrows it — deterministic seeding interacts with quantized kernels + sampler. Could be subtle tokenizer padding -> sampling interplay.

ana: For immediate action: can we gate the canary rollout? This is a release blocker for dedicated deploys that will pick up the kernel.

sara: I put the canary pipeline on hold and rolled forward a stop-gate in the console: https://console.redwood/rollouts/flags/456 (status: paused). :lock:

ops-bot: Auto-alert created: incident/2026-02-24-eval-regression. Assigned to eng-ml oncall.

mike: Next steps propose: 1) revert deterministic_seed default in sampling-service; 2) add a unit test that runs sampling + tokenization under q8 kernels; 3) run full bisect to confirm root cause. Thoughts?

jules: I'll open a PR to revert the default immediately and add a reproducer test. If that fixes local runs, we can unpause after CI verifies.

ana: Meanwhile, I'll do a quick git bisect across the quant/kernel PRs to be certain there isn't another contributor. Command I'll run:```\ngit bisect start HEAD origin/main\n# good = origin/main@stable-quant\n# bad = HEAD (canary)\n```\n\nana: If bisect points at sampling-service change, we rollback that change. If it points to kernel changes, we may need to pin older kernel in Dedicated.

mike: Agreed. Also add metric-level guard in eval harness: if accuracy_delta < -2.0% and pvalue < 0.01 mark as blocker and prevent auto-rollout. That would stop future surprises.

jules: PR 3124 opened: revert default seeding + test. CI triggered. Link: https://phab.redwood/D3124. I'll monitor.

ci-bot: Build D3124 status: running (unit tests + quant smoke).

ana: Thanks. If D3124 passes, can we re-run canary with both seeds (0 and None) and compare diffs? Want to ensure parity and not hide nondeterminism.

mike: Yes. Also add a quick eval checklist entry: "verify seeding behavior across quant levels".

sara: Noted — I've added a ticket to the release checklist and notified sales/CS about canary pause (so they don't expect upgrades this week).

jules: CI green on D3124 (unit + smoke passed). Pushed a canary rerun.

ci-bot: Canary run finished. artifact: https://ci.internal/redwood/canary/1764201123/rerun. Summary: accuracy_delta = -0.3% (seed None), -0.4% (seed 0). Regression resolved within threshold.

ana: Great. Closing incident after we let canary sit for 24h. Leave the sampling default reverted until we add explicit config and docs.

mike: Postmortem action items: add targeted tests for sampling+tokenization+quant kernels, add eval harness guard threshold, and document seeding semantics for private deployments.

ana: Thanks everyone. Good catch. :thumbsup:
